channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Goldman's Oppenheimer Sees Opportunity to Diversify
item.description: Peter Oppenheimer, chief global equity strategist at Goldman Sachs, says that equity market volatility will continue "for some time" but that is an environment which creates opportunities. "Investors should be broadly diversified, and that's true within equities and indeed across asset classes," Oppenheimer tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cassava Seeks $1 Billion for Nvidia Chips to Power AI in Africa
item.description: Cassava Technologies Ltd. is seeking to raise as much as $1 billion to buy Nvidia Corp. chips to power its African artificial-intelligence data centers, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Loni Prinsloo

item.title: Clampdown on China Chip Loophole Puts Billions in Loans at Risk
item.description: Banks and private credit funds that lent billions to fund data centers and AI chip purchases in Southeast Asia are being forced to confront a long-feared scenario: the loss of critical Chinese customers.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: SAP Executive Thomas Saueressig Quits to Become Ionos CEO
item.description: SAP SE executive board member and Chief Customer Officer Thomas Saueressig resigned to become chief executive officer of Ionos Group SE.
item.dc:creator: Christina Kyriasoglou

item.title: US Moves to Curb China’s Remote Access to Nvidia’s Chips
item.description: The Trump administration moved to restrict foreign countries from giving Chinese companies remote access to advanced AI chips and servers, amid scrutiny over its semiconductor export controls following an alleged Nvidia espionage scandal. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Vance Says US Won’t Stay in Iran War for Years as Oil Drops on Supply Recovery
item.description: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Markets Await Nvidia Earnings Call for Clues on Strategy
item.description: Nvidia’s earnings arrive at perhaps the strangest time possible for the world’s most important artificial intelligence chipmaker. The company reports its results after the market closes Tuesday, but its performance in the latest quarter is being overshadowed by last week’s ouster of CEO Jensen Huang. Bloomberg's Anthony Stephens has a preview. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Chip Curbs Force Xi to Weigh Response Before Trump Summit
item.description: The US’s sweeping new restrictions on China’s access to high-end AI chips present Xi Jinping with a dilemma just days before he meets Donald Trump: Hit back hard enough to threaten a fragile trade truce, or play it cool and take action later.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Kenya Signs $692 Million Deal with Amaco Energy for Gas Plant
item.description: Kenya has signed a deal with AMACO Energy SA for a liquefied natural gas electricity plant to power an upcoming industrial complex near the Mombasa port.
item.dc:creator: David Herbling

item.title: Finland’s Iceye Bids €2 Billion for Rocket-Launch Firm Avio
item.description: Finland’s Iceye Oy made a €2.05 billion ($2.26 billion) offer for Italian rocket maker Avio SpA, in a proposal that would speed consolidation in Europe’s space and defense sectors.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Brambilla and Kati Pohjanpalo

item.title: Breaking Down the US Move to Curb Remote Access to Chips
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Analyst Rob Lea discusses US concerns about the Chinese AI sector as the Trump administration moves to limit several countries from providing Chinese companies remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers. Several Southeast Asian nations, along with Brazil, will need a US government license to purchase advanced AI chips from Nvidia Corp. and other American manufacturers, according to an interim rule released by the US Commerce Department. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Removes More Explicit Instagram Posts Under India Scrutiny
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. removed more explicit content from Instagram in India, after a series of lapses brought the social media giant under tougher scrutiny across the country of over half a billion users.
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Ng

item.title: Baidu’s Robin Li Says AI Needs Monetization to Avoid Bubble Risk
item.description: Baidu Inc. chief Robin Li sees an increasingly urgent need for better monetization of artificial intelligence if heavy investments in the technology are to pay off.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Impact of US Move to Curb Chip Access
item.description: Managing Editor for Asian Equities at Bloomberg News Lianting Tu says tighter access to chips could constrain AI model training in China and potentially slow sales growth for AI cloud businesses. That could have a knock-on effect on data-center expansion and demand for Chinese hardware companies, some of which supply Nvidia, as the Trump administration moves to limit countries from providing Chinese companies remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: APEC's Pedrosa on Shenzhen Summit Expectations
item.description: Eduardo Pedrosa, Executive Director for the APEC Secretariat, discusses his expectations for a highly-anticipated APEC Summit in Shenzhen, where leaders of the APEC economies, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, will meet to discuss economic, technology and trade issues. He speaks with Stephen Engle on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China AI Star Sinks 85% From Peak as Chip Fears Hit Model Makers
item.description: Few stocks rode China’s artificial intelligence frenzy as spectacularly as model developer Z.AI Co. Now, its dramatic reversal is laying bare the vulnerabilities facing the country’s AI upstarts.
item.dc:creator: Jeanny Yu

item.title: Pimco Sees Data Center Spreads Tightening Versus Tech Debt
item.description: Spreads on bonds financing artificial intelligence data centers may tighten relative to debt issued by the technology companies that use the facilities, as slower construction curbs new issuance, according to Pacific Investment Management Co.
item.dc:creator: Harry Suhartono

item.title: More Volatility Forecast for AI as Nvidia Earnings Loom
item.description:
Xi Qiao, UBS financial advisor and managing director, said Nvidia faces a particularly difficult backdrop ahead of earnings, including tougher U.S. export restrictions and concerns surrounding Jensen Huang. Qiao expects near-term volatility in Nvidia and the broader AI trade, as markets brace for slower investment in the AI ecosystem and possible supply-chain disruptions. Qiao advised investors to stay invested while diversifying across sectors, regions and asset classes.
Original filename: 20261117_004905_Xi_Qiao_Sees_More_Volatility_Ahead_of_Nvidia_Earnings.mp4 (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tripadvisor Loan Soars as $600 Million Payment Boosts Confidence
item.description: Tripadvisor Inc.’s loan soared Monday as the company repaid $600 million of debt using proceeds of a sale, easing concerns for lenders as it faces a major leadership change and challenges from generative artificial intelligence tools.
item.dc:creator: Dorothy Ma and Katherine Schwartz

item.title: Asia’s Data Center Hotbed Hit by US Chip Curbs as Trump Visits
item.description: President Donald Trump is targeting Southeast Asia in Washington’s rush to tighten China’s access to the world’s most advanced chips, with his administration announcing new rules just before he arrives in the region.
item.dc:creator: Ramsey Al-Rikabi and Philip J. Heijmans
